subject: biology
title: The nervous system
key_idea: The **nervous system** lets the body detect a stimulus and respond quickly. Receptors send **electrical impulses** along neurones to the central nervous system. It coordinates the response and sends impulses to effectors. Neurones are joined by **synapses**, where a chemical carries the signal.

blocks.text: The nervous system lets humans react to their surroundings and coordinate their behaviour. This section covers the main parts and the order they work in.

items.meaning: A change in the surroundings that is detected.
A cell that detects a stimulus. Receptors are found in sense organs.
The brain and the spinal cord. It coordinates the response.
A muscle or a gland that carries out the response.
A nerve cell that carries information as electrical impulses.

items: Light is detected by receptors in the **eye**.
Chemicals (taste) are detected by receptors in the **tongue**.
Sound is detected by receptors in the **ear**.
Muscles respond by contracting. Glands respond by secreting hormones.
Reflex actions use the same pathway but do not involve the conscious part of the brain. They are covered separately.

diagram.alt: A flow diagram of the nervous pathway: stimulus, receptor, sensory neurone, central nervous system, motor neurone, effector, response.

items: Information passes from receptor to CNS to effector.
The CNS is the brain and spinal cord.
Information travels along neurones as electrical impulses.

blocks.text: Three types of neurone carry impulses through the pathway. Each has a different job.

rows: From a receptor to the CNS
Takes information about a stimulus into the CNS.
Inside the CNS (brain or spinal cord)
Connects a sensory neurone to a motor neurone.
From the CNS to an effector
Tells a muscle to contract or a gland to secrete.

blocks.text: How a motor neurone is adapted

items: It is **long**, so it carries impulses a long way from the CNS to a muscle.
It has **branches**, so it can reach several muscle cells.
It has an insulating fatty sheath (the **myelin sheath**), so impulses travel faster.
It has many mitochondria, which release energy by respiration for the impulse to travel.
It is narrow, so many neurones fit in a small space.

blocks.text: Convert units first. A distance in mm must be changed to m, and a time in s changed to ms by multiplying by 1000.

diagram.alt: A practice question: calculate how long an impulse takes to travel along a neurone, in milliseconds.
diagram.question: A nerve impulse travels at {v} m/s along a neurone that is {d} m long. Calculate the time taken, in milliseconds.
working: Rearrange the equation: time = distance ÷ speed.
Multiply by 1000 to change seconds to milliseconds. The answer is {answer} ms.

items: Sensory, relay, motor: receptor to CNS, inside the CNS, CNS to effector.
A motor neurone is long and often has an insulating sheath.
Impulses are fast: up to about 100 m/s.

blocks.text: Neurones do not touch. A small gap called a synapse separates them. An electrical impulse cannot cross it, so a chemical carries the message.

items.text: An electrical impulse reaches the end of the first neurone.
The impulse causes the release of a chemical, a **neurotransmitter**.
The neurotransmitter diffuses across the gap.
It binds to receptors on the next neurone and triggers an electrical impulse there.

items: In a neurone, information is carried as an **electrical impulse**.
Across a synapse, information is carried as a **chemical** that diffuses.
A drug that stops neurotransmitters binding to receptors stops the impulse in the next neurone. Some painkillers work this way, so the pain is not felt.
The nervous system uses electrical impulses along neurones. The response is fast and short-lived.
The endocrine (hormonal) system uses hormones carried in the blood. The response is slower and lasts longer.
A synapse is a gap between two neurones.
Electrical impulse, then chemical across the gap, then electrical impulse.
Nerves are faster than hormones.

checks.q: Name the two parts of the central nervous system.
checks.a: The brain and the spinal cord.

checks.q: Describe how information is passed across a synapse.
checks.a: The impulse causes the release of a neurotransmitter. It diffuses across the gap and triggers an electrical impulse in the next neurone.

checks.q: A nerve impulse travels at 100 m/s along a neurone 1.2 m long. Calculate the time taken in milliseconds.

worked_example.question:
Motor neurones are involved in reactions.

Explain one way the motor neurone cell is adapted for its function.
answer_points: From the CNS (brain or spinal cord) to a muscle or effector.
worked_example.tip: Each approach is worth three linked marks: the feature, what it does, and why it helps. Other features that score are branches, many mitochondria, an insulating sheath and being narrow.

worked_example.question: Explain how impulses are transmitted at synapses.
answer_points: A synapse is a gap between neurones.
The (electrical) impulse stimulates the release of a chemical.
The chemical is a neurotransmitter, which diffuses across the gap (synapse).
It stimulates an (electrical) impulse in the next neurone.
worked_example.tip: Five points are available and the question is worth four marks. Name the neurotransmitter step and say that it diffuses.

items.meaning: A fibre that carries impulses towards the cell body of a neurone.
A long fibre that carries impulses away from the cell body.
A fatty layer around an axon that insulates it and speeds up impulses.

blocks.text: Most neurones in the brain are unmyelinated. They connect to other neurones nearby. Motor neurones are myelinated because they send impulses further, from the CNS to effectors.

worked_example.question:
Hormones are part of the endocrine system.

Describe two differences between the endocrine system and the nervous system.
answer_points: The endocrine system uses hormones (chemical messengers) but the nervous system uses nerve impulses (electrical messages).
The endocrine system is slower acting. Its responses are longer-lived. It communicates via the blood but the nervous system uses neurones.
worked_example.tip: Any two differences from the list score. The slower-acting and longer-lived points can be given the other way round for the nervous system.

worked_example.question: Describe how the events that occur at a synapse generate an impulse in the next neurone.
answer_points: The neurotransmitter is released from vesicles in the first neurone into the synaptic gap.
The neurotransmitter molecules diffuse across the gap.
They bind to receptor proteins on the next neurone, which stimulates an impulse.
worked_example.tip: Any three points score. Name the neurotransmitter, the diffusion and the binding to receptors.

blocks.text: The nervous system has two parts. The CNS is the brain and spinal cord.

items: The **peripheral nervous system (PNS)** is the nerves outside the brain and spinal cord.
The PNS links the receptors and effectors to the CNS.

blocks.text: (Supplement) A synapse has three main features.

items: The first neurone has **vesicles** that contain neurotransmitter molecules.
The **synaptic gap** is the space between the two neurones.
The next neurone has **receptor proteins** that the neurotransmitter binds to.

blocks.text: (Supplement) Only the first neurone releases neurotransmitter, and only the next neurone has receptors. So a synapse makes impulses travel in one direction only.
A **sense organ** is a group of receptor cells that respond to a specific stimulus.

items: Light: the eye.
Sound: the ear.
Touch and temperature: the skin.
Chemicals: the tongue and nose.

worked_example.question: Give three differences between hormones and neurotransmitters.
answer_points: Hormones are produced in endocrine glands. Neurotransmitters are produced in the first (presynaptic) neurone.
Hormones are carried in the blood. Neurotransmitters pass across a synapse.
Hormones affect many target cells all around the body. Neurotransmitters affect one cell.
Hormones give a long-term effect. Neurotransmitters give a short-term effect.
worked_example.tip: Any three differences score one mark each. Write both sides of each difference.
